content.value_statement: Python code can drift into mutable models, unclear errors, and inconsistent type checking. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for safer Python structure.
actual_capabilities: Recommends frozen dataclasses for immutable domain models.
Shows discriminated unions with Literal for request states.
Uses NewType to separate domain identifiers.
Promotes Protocol classes for structural typing.
Documents exception chaining and structured logging patterns.
Suggests optional ty, pyright, and mypy type-checking choices.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not run checks by itself.
It does not replace a full security or architecture review.
The ty tool advice depends on current project constraints.
Examples are concise and may need adaptation for older Python versions.

use_cases.title: Strengthen Domain Models
use_cases.description: Refactor service objects toward immutable dataclasses, clear identifiers, and explicit state variants.

use_cases.title: Review Python Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check whether changes use clear types, preserve exception context, and log structured values.

use_cases.title: Choose Type-Checking Workflows
use_cases.description: Compare ty, pyright, and mypy for local development, editor support, and CI speed.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Python File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-best-practices skill to review this Python file. Identify simple type, error handling, and logging improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Domain Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the python-best-practices skill to improve these domain models. Prefer immutable data, specific identifiers, and explicit state representation.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Errors and Logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python workflow for exception chaining and structured logging. Explain changes that preserve context and improve observability.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Typed Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the python-best-practices skill to design a typed Python workflow for this feature. Include domain primitives, state handling, and type-checker guidance.

output_examples.input: Review a service module that mixes user IDs and order IDs as plain strings.
output: Use separate domain identifier types for user and order values.
Add typed function boundaries so incorrect identifiers are caught earlier.
Keep runtime validation where data enters from external systems.

output_examples.input: Improve error reporting for a JSON parsing path.
output_examples.output: The response recommends preserving the original JSON decoding error with exception chaining and returning a clearer validation message.

output_examples.input: Choose a type checker for a large CI pipeline.
output: Consider ty for fast CI feedback.
Use pyright when editor inference is a priority.
Use mypy when plugin support is required.

best_practices: Ask the agent to explain which Python version assumptions it uses.
Run type checking only after approving external commands.
Pair the guidance with project-specific lint and test rules.
anti_patterns: Applying every example without considering project Python version.
Replacing tests with type hints alone.
Letting an agent run `uvx` commands without confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It contains an optional type-checker command example, but command execution requires the host agent or user.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it enforce formatting?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on type modeling, error handling, logging, and type-checker selection.

faq.question: Is ty required?
faq.answer: No. The skill presents ty as an optional fast type checker, alongside pyright and mypy.

faq.question: Can it help with legacy Python?
faq.answer: Yes. Some examples use modern syntax and may need adaptation for older Python versions.

faq.question: Is it a security skill?
faq.answer: No. It supports safer code style, but it is categorized as coding guidance.
